svg.title: Cliff erosion at Aldbrough, Holderness, between LIDAR surveys in 2008 and 2023
svg.desc: Map of elevation change between two Environment Agency LIDAR surveys of 1.1 kilometres of the Holderness coast. The cliff retreated 22.7 metres on average, 1.55 metres a year, and up to 38.2 metres, with a chart of retreat along the frontage.
svg.text: Cliff erosion at Aldbrough, Holderness: LIDAR 2008 against LIDAR 2023
Section A to B, next figure
Retreat of the cliff face on 53 transects, 20 m apart (m)
Change is the 2023 survey minus the 2008 survey on a 1 m grid. Changes under 0.5 m, and ground below 1 m in both surveys (sea and wet sand), are left blank.
The cliff face is the 8 m contour. Beach levels also move with season and tide. Derived by Beck & Call Digital from Environment Agency time-stamped LIDAR DTM tiles.
